pc-fun-s04-cp2-002: ln(x) is defined only for x > 0, so its domain is (0, ∞).
ln(1) = 0, so the graph passes through (1, 0).
The other choices fail: eˣ and sin(x) are defined for all reals, and 1/x is defined for x < 0 too. So the function is f(x) = ln(x).
pc-fun-s04-cp2-004: |x| ≥ 0 for every x, and every nonnegative value is reached, so the range is [0, ∞).
The graph of |x| is two rays meeting at the origin: a V shape.
x² also has range [0, ∞) but is a U-shaped curve, so the function is f(x) = |x|.

pc-fun-s04-cp2-008: e^x is always positive and takes every positive value, so its range is (0, ∞).
e⁰ = 1, so the graph passes through (0, 1).

pc-fun-s04-cp1-002: sin(x) and cos(x) both stay between -1 and 1.
sin(0) = 0, so sin passes through the origin; cos(0) = 1, so cos does not.
pc-fun-s04-cp1-004: ln(x) is defined only for x > 0, so its domain is (0, ∞).

pc-fun-s04-cp1-006: x³ is odd: (-x)³ = -x³, so its graph is symmetric about the origin.
Its graph rises from left to right everywhere, so it is increasing on all reals, and 1³ = 1 puts (1, 1) on it.
The other choices fail: x² and √x are not odd, and sin(x) is odd but not increasing on all reals. So the function is f(x) = x³.

pc-gtt-s06-cp2-001: The altitude from C is perpendicular to side c, forming a right triangle with hypotenuse b and angle A.
In that right triangle, sin A = opposite/hypotenuse = h/b.
pc-gtt-s06-cp2-003: Start from the Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab·cos C.
Move the cosine term: 2ab·cos C = a² + b² - c².
Divide by 2ab: cos C = (a² + b² - c²) ÷ (2ab).
pc-gtt-s06-cp2-005: Expand: a² = b²cos²A - 2bc·cos A + c² + b²sin²A.
Group: a² = b²(sin²A + cos²A) + c² - 2bc·cos A.
The identity sin²A + cos²A = 1 simplifies this to the Law of Cosines a² = b² + c² - 2bc·cos A.
pc-gtt-s06-cp2-007: So c² = a² + b², the Pythagorean Theorem.
pc-gtt-s06-cp1-001: Both expressions equal h, so b·sin A = a·sin B.
Divide both sides by sin A·sin B: b/sin B = a/sin A.
So a/sin A = b/sin B, the Law of Sines.
pc-gtt-s06-cp1-003: C is b units from A (side b = AC), at angle A above the x-axis.
Its x-coordinate is b·cos A and its y-coordinate is b·sin A.
pc-gtt-s06-honors-001: Take side a as the base. The height is the perpendicular distance from the opposite vertex to side a.
That height is the leg opposite angle C in a right triangle with hypotenuse b, so it equals b·sin C.
Area = (1/2)(a)(b·sin C) = (1/2)ab·sin C, so the height is b·sin C.
pc-gtt-s06-honors-003: Solving sin B = (b·sin A)/a gives one value of sin B between 0 and 1.
Two angles in (0°, 180°) have that sine: B and 180° - B, because sin θ = sin(180° - θ).
If both angles fit in a triangle with A, there are two possible triangles.
